pcp_per100k.label: Primary care doctors per 100,000 people
pcp_per100k.source: HRSA Area Health Resources Files (American Medical Association Physician Masterfile), via County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
pcp_per100k.vintage: CHR&R Supplemental Data Release, March 25, 2026; pulled 2026-11-18; earlier years from the CHR&R 2025 trends file
pcp_per100k.note: Practicing non-federal doctors (M.D. and D.O.) under age 75 in general practice, family medicine, general internal medicine and general pediatrics, per 100,000 residents. Counted where the doctor practices, so people may get care in a nearby county.

dentists_per100k.label: Dentists per 100,000 people
dentists_per100k.source: HRSA Area Health Resources Files (CMS National Provider Identifier file), via County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
dentists_per100k.vintage: CHR&R Supplemental Data Release, March 25, 2026; pulled 2026-11-18; earlier years from the CHR&R 2025 trends file
dentists_per100k.note: Dentists with a National Provider Identifier, per 100,000 residents. Some may no longer practice or take new patients.

mh_providers_per100k.label: Mental health providers per 100,000 people
mh_providers_per100k.source: CMS National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPI file), via County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
mh_providers_per100k.vintage: CHR&R Supplemental Data Release, March 25, 2026; pulled 2026-11-18
mh_providers_per100k.note: Psychiatrists, psychologists, licensed clinical social workers, counselors, marriage and family therapists, addiction counselors and mental health nurse practitioners with an NPI, per 100,000 residents. Some may no longer practice or take new patients.

suicide_rate.label: Suicide deaths per 100,000 people (age-adjusted)
suicide_rate.source: CDC National Center for Health Statistics mortality files, via County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
suicide_rate.vintage: CHR&R Supplemental Data Release, March 25, 2026; pulled 2026-11-18
suicide_rate.note: Suicide deaths per 100,000 people, age-adjusted, five years combined, by the county where the person lived. Left blank when there were fewer than 20 deaths in the five years.

traffic_deaths_per100k.label: Traffic deaths per 100,000 people
traffic_deaths_per100k.source: NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS); Census Bureau population estimates
traffic_deaths_per100k.vintage: FARS final files 2015-2023; population Vintage 2025 (2020 on) and 2010-2020 intercensal estimates; pulled 2026-11-18
traffic_deaths_per100k.note: Deaths in motor vehicle crashes on public roads, counted in the county where the crash happened, per 100,000 residents per year, five years combined. Not age-adjusted. Left blank when there were fewer than 20 deaths in the five years.

library_spend_per_capita.label: Public library spending per person
library_spend_per_capita.source: Institute of Museum and Library Services, Public Libraries Survey; Census Bureau population estimates
library_spend_per_capita.vintage: FY 2019-FY 2024 public-use files (imputed); FY 2024 file released 2026; pulled 2026-11-18
library_spend_per_capita.note: Total operating spending by public library systems (staff, materials and other costs; not building projects), in dollars of that year, per resident. Most Georgia library systems serve several counties. Each system's total is split among the counties where it has a library building, by population, so every county in a regional system shows that system's per-person figure. The Georgia figure adds up all Georgia systems.

library_visits_per_capita.label: Public library visits per person
library_visits_per_capita.source: Institute of Museum and Library Services, Public Libraries Survey; Census Bureau population estimates
library_visits_per_capita.vintage: FY 2019-FY 2024 public-use files (imputed); FY 2024 file released 2026; pulled 2026-11-18
library_visits_per_capita.note: In-person visits to public libraries in a year, per resident. Some libraries count every visit; others estimate from a typical week. Most Georgia library systems serve several counties. Each system's total is split among the counties where it has a library building, by population, so every county in a regional system shows that system's per-person figure. The Georgia figure adds up all Georgia systems.

social_associations_per10k.label: Membership groups per 10,000 people
social_associations_per10k.source: Census Bureau County Business Patterns; Census Bureau population estimates (definition from County Health Rankings & Roadmaps)
social_associations_per10k.vintage: CBP 2019-2023 (2023 is the latest year released); pulled 2026-11-18
social_associations_per10k.note: Places of worship, civic and social clubs, unions, business and professional groups, political groups, sports clubs, golf and country clubs, fitness centers and bowling alleys with paid staff, per 10,000 residents. Census leaves out any industry with fewer than 3 such places in a county, so small counties are undercounted a little. Georgia's figure is the sum of the county counts, built the same way as the counties; Census's statewide count, which includes the places withheld in county cells, gives 8.7.

voter_turnout.label: Voter turnout, 2024 presidential election
voter_turnout.source: Georgia Secretary of State official results, as compiled by the MIT Election Data + Science Lab; Census Bureau American Community Survey
voter_turnout.vintage: MEDSL 2024 precinct returns (Georgia file dated 2026-04-28); ACS 2020-2024 5-year table B29001; pulled 2026-11-18
voter_turnout.note: Votes cast for president divided by U.S. citizens age 18 and older. Ballots left blank for president are not counted. The citizen count is a survey estimate, and it includes some people who cannot vote, such as people serving a felony prison term.
